page: Amazon Web Services r7a.48xlarge is a memory-optimized server instance powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It features 192 dedicated physical cores on an x86_64 architecture, utilizing AMD EPYC 9R14 processors running at a clock speed of 3.7 GHz. The system is equipped with 1536.0 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 5 GHz, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local storage or GPU accelerators, but offers a baseline network bandwidth of 50 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier multi-core CPU performance, with stress-ng multi-core and PassMark CPU scores placing in the top 10%. The DDR5 memory subsystem delivers top-tier read and write bandwidth for both small cached and large uncached blocks. In database and memory-bound workloads, the instance achieves top-tier throughput in Redis SET operations and static web serving, alongside strong performance in PassMark database operations.

While prompt processing for large language models registers as strong to top-tier, text generation speeds for smaller models represent a performance tradeoff, falling into the bottom 25%. The absence of local NVMe storage requires reliance on network-attached storage, which may impact I/O-heavy tasks. This hardware profile is suited for memory-intensive applications, large-scale database deployments, software compilation, and memory-bound enterprise workloads that leverage high-density DDR5 RAM and massive parallel CPU execution.
